_about: Held-out retrieval set: made-up personal data, written after pal's cut-offs were tuned and never used to tune anything. Nothing here is about a real person. Each query's `expect` lists the corpus ids that answer it; `answer`, when given, must appear in the returned passage itself (for documents: the right chunk, not just the right file). Queries with an empty `expect` have no answer stored; `type` says whether they are off-topic or a near miss (the topic is stored, the asked-for fact is not).

documents.text:
# Home insurance policy summary

Policy number HP-558201, held with Maple Mutual. Coverage runs for one year and renews on July 1. The renewal notice arrives by email about thirty days before.

## Deductible
The standard deductible is 1,000 dollars per claim. For sewer backup claims the deductible rises to 2,500 dollars. The deductible is taken off the payout, not billed separately.

## What is covered
Contents are covered up to 60,000 dollars at replacement cost. Personal liability coverage is 2 million dollars and applies anywhere in the world. Additional living expenses are paid for up to 12 months if the unit cannot be lived in after a covered loss.

## Water damage
Sudden and accidental water damage, such as a burst pipe or a washing machine hose that fails, is covered. Damage from a gradual leak that went on for weeks, such as a slow drip under a sink, is not covered, because it is treated as a maintenance problem. Flood from surface water is excluded unless the overland water endorsement is added, which this policy does not have.

## Valuables
Jewellery and watches are limited to 5,000 dollars in total unless they are listed separately. Bicycles are limited to 2,000 dollars each. Laptops and phones are covered as ordinary contents.

## Making a claim
Report a claim within 30 days of discovering the damage. Take photos before cleaning up, keep damaged items until the adjuster has seen them, and keep receipts for any emergency repairs. Claims can be opened online or by phone, around the clock.

# Lisbon trip, May

## Flights
Outbound flight AC 832 leaves Toronto on May 3 at 21:40 and lands in Lisbon the next morning at 09:55. The return flight is on May 10, leaving Lisbon at 12:15. Seats 23A and 23B are booked on both legs; checked bags are included.

## Where we're staying
Casa do Bairro, a guesthouse in Alfama, for all six nights. Check-in is from 14:00; they will hold bags if we arrive early. The nearest tram stop is on the 28 line, two minutes up the hill.

## Plans by day
May 4: arrive, sleep, an easy walk along the river in the evening.
May 5: Belém in the morning for the monastery and the tower. Dinner reservation at Taberna da Rua das Flores at 20:00, under Jonah's name.
May 6: day trip to Sintra by train from Rossio station. Pena Palace tickets are for the 10:30 entry slot, so take the 8:41 train.
May 7: pastry class in the afternoon, 15:00 to 17:30, at a cooking school in Príncipe Real. It covers pastéis de nata from scratch.
May 8: free day; maybe the tile museum.
May 9: LX Factory and a last dinner somewhere near the hotel.

## Money and practical bits
Most places take cards, but small cafés may want cash, so take out about 100 euros on arrival. Tipping is small, around five to ten percent at restaurants. Buy a Viva Viagem card at the airport metro station for trams and trains.

# Employee benefits summary

## Health
Prescription drugs are covered at 90 percent with a pay-direct card. Paramedical services such as massage, physiotherapy and chiropractic share a combined maximum of 500 dollars per person per year, with no referral needed.

## Dental
Basic dental work such as cleanings, fillings and check-ups is covered at 80 percent. Major dental work such as crowns, bridges and dentures is covered at 50 percent. The annual dental maximum is 2,000 dollars per person. Orthodontics is not covered.

## Vision
Glasses or contact lenses are covered up to 300 dollars every two years. One eye exam is covered every two years as well.

## Retirement savings
The company matches RRSP contributions up to 4 percent of salary. Matching starts after three months of employment, and the match vests immediately.

## Leave
Parental leave is topped up to 85 percent of salary for the first six months. There are five paid personal days a year in addition to vacation, and they do not carry over.

## Support
The employee assistance program offers free, confidential counselling, up to eight sessions per issue, by phone or video. It also covers legal and financial advice calls.

# Team onboarding guide

## Shipping code
Every pull request needs two approvals before it can be merged, and at least one approver should be from outside the author's pod. CI must be green; flaky tests are retried once automatically and then fail the build.

We deploy to production on Tuesdays and Thursdays, after the 11:00 stand-up. There is a code freeze from Friday at 14:00 until Monday morning, so nothing merges to main over the weekend except hotfixes approved by the on-call engineer.

## On-call
The on-call rotation is weekly and hands over on Mondays at 10:00. New team members shadow one full rotation before they join it. The on-call engineer carries the pager, triages alerts within 15 minutes during the day and 30 minutes at night, and writes the weekly handover note.

## Incident severity
Sev 1: the product is down or data is at risk; page the incident commander immediately. Sev 2: a major feature is broken for many users; fix within a working day. Sev 3: a minor bug or a single customer affected; goes into the normal backlog.

Every Sev 1 and Sev 2 gets a blameless review within five working days. The review lists what happened, what we learned, and follow-up tickets with owners.

## Meetings
Planning happens every second Monday. Retros are on alternate Fridays. Demo day is the last Thursday of each month, and anyone can present.

# Brompton care notes

## Tyres
Keep the tyres at 100 psi for everyday commuting. Riders over 80 kg can go up to 110 psi. Check the pressure every week; small wheels lose air faster than big ones and soft tyres pinch-flat easily on curbs.

## Folding
Fold order: swing the rear wheel under the frame, unclip and fold the front wheel alongside, drop the handlebar stem, then lower the saddle all the way to lock the fold. Unfold in the opposite order. Always check the hinge clamps are fully tight before riding.

## Chain and gears
Clean and lube the chain every 300 km, or after any ride in the rain. Use a dry lube in summer and a wet lube in winter. The hub gears should be serviced by a shop once a year; if gears start slipping, the indicator chain on the right side probably needs adjusting.

## Brakes
Brake pads last roughly 2,000 km of city riding. Replace them when the grooves are worn flat. Rim brakes squeal when wet; that is normal.

## Limits
Maximum rider weight is 110 kg, and the front carrier block takes bags up to 10 kg. The bike should not be left folded outside in the rain for long, because water collects in the frame hinge.

# 10K training plan, spring

Goal race: the Harbourfront 10K on June 14, aiming for under 50 minutes. That is an average pace of 5:00 per kilometre.

## Weekly structure
Tuesday: tempo run, 20 to 30 minutes at about 4:50 per kilometre after a warm-up.
Thursday: intervals, such as 6 x 800 m at 4:30 pace with 90 seconds of easy jogging between them.
Sunday: long run, starting at 10 km in week one and building to 14 km by week six, all at an easy, conversational pace around 6:00 per kilometre.
The other days are rest or easy cross-training; Wednesday soccer counts as the cross-training day.

## Taper
Week eight is the taper: cut total distance by about 40 percent, keep one short tempo session, and do nothing hard in the last three days before the race.

## Race day
Eat breakfast three hours before the start: oatmeal and a banana. Warm up for 15 minutes. Start slightly slower than goal pace for the first two kilometres, then settle in. Take water at the 5 km station.

## If something hurts
A sore calf or ankle means an extra rest day, not pushing through. If pain lasts more than a week, book a session with the physio.

messages.content: Can you remind me why we picked the guesthouse in Alfama over the hotel in Baixa?
You said Alfama was quieter at night, and the Baixa hotel had no elevator, which mattered because of Jonah's knee.
Dev mentioned he'd love a good pair of compression socks for his long shifts at the hospital.
Noted: compression socks for Dev, for the long nursing shifts.
I rolled my left ankle at soccer last night. Should I ice it?
Yes: rest it, ice for 15 to 20 minutes at a time, and keep it raised. If it still hurts to walk on in a few days, see your physiotherapist.
For the condo board: the reserve fund is at 312,000 after paying for the roof repair.
Got it, the reserve fund stands at 312,000 after the roof repair.
